subject: Your plugin.json census + our Codex plugin data
text:
Hi there,

I've been poking around agentpluginsdirectory.com and the validator is really handy. Checking every manifest against the 1.0.0 schema before listing it is the right call.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. We ran similar checks on 339 open-source plugins (manifest errors, licenses, stars, how many READMEs have no install command) and published it here: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's CC BY, so feel free to cite it next to your stats page if it's useful. And if you'd be up for a simple link swap between the two directories, I'm happy to add yours to our list of plugin directories.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

site: Agent Plugins Directory by Ronny Badilla (agent-plugins.directory)
subject: agent-plugins.directory + PickAPlugin
text:
Hi Ronny,

I read your about page and liked the "nothing is submitted and nothing is approved" approach. Letting the indexer decide keeps it honest.

I run PickAPlugin, a much smaller, hand-sorted directory of Codex and ChatGPT plugins, so we're kind of the opposite approach. I think the two fit together well. Would you be open to linking to each other? Happy to add it to our page of plugin directories too.

We also published some open data on 339 plugins (licenses, stars, plugin.json errors) that's free to cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Codex plugin data for your field guides
text:
Hi MCPNav team,

I like that you keep featured spots editorial and say so right on the submit page. Not many directories do that.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. We pulled GitHub data on 339 open-source plugins, including how many wire up a remote MCP server and how many READMEs mention an API key: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's free to cite with credit if it fits one of your field guides. Happy to link to MCPNav from our side too.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Security-ish data on 339 Codex plugins
text:
Hi Agent Skills Hub team,

Your point that stars alone are a weak signal is exactly what we found too. I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins, and we ran pre-install style checks on 339 open-source plugins: licenses, archived repos, API key mentions, plugin.json errors.

It's here, CC BY and free to cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

If it's useful as a source on one of your security or trends pages, a credit link would be great. Thanks either way.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Free listing for agent-toolbox on PickAPlugin
text:
Hi Yunseo,

I came across agent-toolbox and liked the provenance tracking. Knowing where a skill came from before installing it is something most registries skip.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of Codex and ChatGPT plugins, and I'd like to give it a free listing. If you'd rather add it yourself, the form is here: https://pickaplugin.com/submit

There's also a free README badge that links to the listing, if you ever want one. No pressure at all.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
